paper.title: Increased Tobacco Use Treatment Engagement in an Inpatient Tobacco Treatment Program.
paper.summary: Hospitalized patients who use tobacco often face barriers to receiving cessation counseling. We evaluated workflow changes designed to improve patient reach. Across 3 years, 8808 patients received counseling. Successful counseling rates increased from 82% to 90% (P < 0.01), without additional staffing. These findings demonstrate practical strategies for expanding inpatient tobacco treatment.

paper.title: Cross-tonal and cross-generational variability of laryngeal contrasts in Shuangfeng Xiang Chinese.
paper.summary: This study reports the acoustic and articulatory correlates of the three-way laryngeal contrasts in Shuangfeng Xiang Chinese, which shows complex co-occurrence patterns with lexical tones. We focused on the acoustic and articulatory correlates of laryngeal contrasts in alveolar plosives in different tonal contexts and how these patterns change across generations of speakers. Voice onset time (VOT), fundamental frequency (f0), vowel quality (F1 and F2), and vocal fold contact quotient (CQ) were measured. Our results showed that distributional patterns of these correlates were both tone-dependent and speaker-generation-specific. Crucially, for the realization of the voiced onset /d/, we observed that while older speakers relied primarily on robust prevoicing (negative VOT) to distinguish /d/ from /t/, younger speakers exhibited reduced prevoicing and instead introduced breathier phonation (lower CQ) as an enhancing correlate. Furthermore, while different correlates jointly maintain the laryngeal contrasts, analyses of effect sizes (Hedges' g) further confirmed that our young-generation speakers realized the voicing contrast via greater phonetic distinctiveness of breathiness than the old-generation speakers. The differing relationships between laryngeal timing and phonatory state suggest an ongoing process of post-tonogenetic onset devoicing, occurring after a full-fledged tonal distinction appears but before onset voicing is completely lost.

paper.title: Fixing Our Focus: Training Attention to Regulate Emotion
paper.summary: Empirical studies have frequently linked negative attentional biases with attentional dysfunction and negative moods; however, far less research has focused on how attentional deployment can be an adaptive strategy that regulates emotional experience. The authors argue that attention may be an invaluable tool for promoting emotion regulation. Accordingly, they present evidence that selective attention to positive information reflects emotion regulation and that regulating attention is a critical component of the emotion regulatory process. Furthermore, attentional regulation can be successfully trained through repeated practice. The authors ultimately propose a model of attention training methodologies integrating attention-dependent emotion regulation strategies with attention networks. Although additional interdisciplinary research is needed to bolster these nascent findings, meditative practices appear to be among the most effective training methodologies in enhancing emotional well-being. Further exploration of the positive and therapeutic qualities of attention warrants the empirical attention of social and personality psychologists.
